bib.title: Towards VQA Models That Can Read

question: Can VQA models answer questions that require reading and reasoning about text in images, and what dataset and architecture are needed to study this?
hypothesis: Baking in specialised components such as OCR, plus a mechanism to copy OCR tokens as answers, lets VQA models read text, which monolithic VQA networks cannot learn from VQA supervision alone.
contributions: A novel dataset (TextVQA) containing questions which require the model to read and reason about the text in the image to be answered.
Look, Read, Reason & Answer (LoRRA): a novel model architecture which explicitly reasons over the outputs from an OCR system when answering questions.
LoRRA outperforms existing state-of-the-art VQA models on TextVQA as well as VQA 2.0.

method.summary: TextVQA is a crowd-sourced dataset of questions on Open Images photos that require reading text. LoRRA adds a frozen Rosetta OCR module to a Pythia v0.3 VQA model: OCR tokens are attended over, and the answer space is extended by M dynamic slots so the model can copy one OCR token as its answer, trained with binary cross-entropy on logits.

datasets.name: TextVQA
datasets.size: 45,336 questions on 28,408 images; 10 human answers per question
datasets.source: Open Images v3 images from text-heavy categories weighted by Rosetta OCR box counts; train and val from Open Images train set, test from Open Images test set; crowd-sourced
datasets.preprocessing: 3-stage pipeline: filter images without text; collect 1-2 questions per image; collect 10 answers. Questions removed when a majority of workers flagged no text, not a question, no reading required, or unanswerable. Hand-crafted known-answer questions used to filter bad annotators. Random train/val split with no image overlap.

datasets.name: VQA 2.0
datasets.preprocessing: Question vocabulary: top ~77k question words in VQA 2.0 (GloVe custom vocabulary)

models.name: LoRRA (Pythia v0.3 + LoRRA)
models.architecture: Attention-based VQA (grid ResNet-152 res-5c 2048D avg-pooled plus Faster-RCNN fc6 region features, fc7 fine-tuned) + OCR attention branch + copy-augmented answer space; fcomb is element-wise product; fMLP is a two-layer feed-forward network over concatenated [fVQA; fOCR]
models.init_from: Pythia v0.1 design with revised hyperparameters; pre-trained GloVe, FastText, ResNet-152, Visual Genome Faster-RCNN
models.vocab: SA: 3996 answers appearing at least twice in train; LA: 8000 most frequent answers
models.context: max question length 14; max OCR tokens 50

other.ordering: OCR attention weights concatenated to attended features to keep token order
other.copy_limit: can copy only a single OCR token; 8.9% of TextVQA questions need multiple OCR tokens

models.name: Pythia (I+Q), BAN (I+Q), Question-only, Image-only, Pythia+O, Pythia+O+C

training.objective: binary cross-entropy on logits over N+M answer slots
training.seq_len: max question length 14, max OCR tokens 50
training.seeds: validation accuracies averaged over 5 runs with different seeds

other.checkpointing: val accuracy computed every 1000th iteration; best-validation model used for test accuracy

inference.decoding: argmax over N+M logits; index > N copies the corresponding OCR token
inference.samples: single prediction per question; val averaged over 5 seeds

metrics.name: VQA accuracy
metrics.definition: VQA accuracy metric of Goyal et al. (10 human answers per question)

eval.protocol: Val accuracy averaged over 5 seeds; test accuracy from best-val checkpoint. Test numbers reported only for some rows.

evidence.quote: We use a learning rate of 5e-2 for all layers except the fc7 layers used for ﬁne-tuning which are trained with 5e-3.

limits: Copy mechanism can output only a single OCR token; 8.9% of questions need several, and multi-token answers are left as future work.
OCR (Rosetta) fails on rotated, unstructured or occluded text; performance depends on OCR quality (App. B).
Large gap remains: 26.56 val vs 85.01 human; the OCR upper bound alone is 37.12.
Test accuracy is reported for only some models in Table 2; hardware type and compute are not stated; no variance is given for the VQA 2.0 gain (+0.5).
Model shows biases such as answering city questions with new york (App. B).
Dated: later text-VQA models (M4C and successors) and end-to-end OCR-free models supersede LoRRA.

terms.definition: Look, Read, Reason & Answer: VQA model with OCR reading component and copy mechanism
Large (8000 most frequent answers) and short (3996 answers appearing at least twice) answer vocabularies

lineage.work: Pythia v0.1: the winning entry to the VQA Challenge 2018
lineage.note: VQA component is based on Pythia v0.1, revised to v0.3

lineage.work: Rosetta: Large scale system for text detection and recognition in images
Bottom-up and top-down attention (Anderson et al.)
Pointer generator / copy mechanisms (Gu 2016, See 2017, Merity 2017)
